title: Polynomial-Time Encoding of a Selected Gate Fragment
statement: Let $\kappa$ be a finite set with decidable equality, let $\ell$ be a natural number, and let $p(\kappa_0,u)$ be a Boolean function of a type $\kappa_0\in\kappa$ and a bit string $u$ of length $\ell$. Let $k(z)\in\kappa$ be a function of bit strings, and let $w(z,j)$ assign a natural number to each bit string and natural number $j$. Suppose that for each $\kappa_0\in\kappa$, the function returning the one-bit indicator of $k(z)=\kappa_0$ is polynomial-time computable, and that for every $j<\ell$, the unary encoding of $w(z,j)$ is polynomial-time computable. Then the function sending $z$ to the binary fragment encoding of the CNF gate for $p(k(z),\cdot)$, with wire indices $w(z,j)$, is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean predicate on $\kappa$ and bit strings of length $\ell$.
A function $k$ from bit strings to $\kappa$.
For every $\kappa_0\in\kappa$, the one-bit indicator of $k(z)=\kappa_0$ is polynomial-time computable.
A wire-index function $w$ from bit strings and natural numbers to natural numbers.
For every $j<\ell$, the unary encoding of $w(z,j)$ is polynomial-time computable.
